heading: The safety training data or objective produces the shallowness
definition: the data or the training objective produces the shallowness.
summary: Independent studies support this: changing only the safety training data, with the objective held fixed, reduces the shallowness in 1-10B autoregressive and diffusion models, and one joint data-and-objective change at 70B points the same way. Theory papers derive the shallowness from standard objectives under idealized assumptions, but no general objective-level mechanism has been established.

suggested_status.by_scale: R2 at 1-10B for the broad training-data contribution, across autoregressive and diffusion settings; R0 at 10-100B for the joint data/objective intervention. Conditional theory is unscaled. No empirical status established below 1B or above 100B.
suggested_status.reason: Independent intervention evidence supports the broad version: fixed-objective response-data changes in HumorReject (arXiv:2501.13677#T5-Illegal-DR, #T5-Illegal-H) and fixed-objective state-coverage changes in diffusion Recovery Alignment (arXiv:2510.00565#r30, #r55). The larger-scale evidence is the joint intervention in DeRTa (arXiv:2407.09121#R3, #R4). counts: versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original=0; versions.V6.studies_by_size records 1-10B and 10-100B coverage. R2 applies to the broad causal contribution of training choices, not to a universally established objective-level gradient mechanism.
suggested_status.open_questions: A fixed-data objective ablation that measures gradients, positional safety depth and attack robustness would strengthen the objective-specific explanation. Replication of the larger-scale intervention with data and objective separated would change its scale-specific status.

source.title: Fine-tuning aligned language models compromises safety
source.authors: Xiangyu Qi; Yi Zeng; Tinghao Xie; Pin-Yu Chen; Ruoxi Jia; Prateek Mittal; Peter Henderson

original_result.result: The original paper did not test what causes the shallowness.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Refuse-at-any-position training raised the share of LLaMA3-70B's refusals starting mid-response from 20% to 50-55%.
Replacing refusals with humorous replies raised Llama3-8B's prefill-attack safe-response rate from about 3% to 95%.
DPO and NPO safety tuning changed next-token distributions mainly at the first few response tokens.
Diffusion LMs whose safety training lacked partly generated responses with harmful tokens kept 22-28% attack success.
Under idealized assumptions, a theorem shows SFT and DPO suppress gradients at later response tokens.
Theory: zero harm gradient past the harm-determining prefix; author argues shallowness is the objective's optimum.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An empirical demonstration that changing only the objective, with training data held fixed, changes measured gradient concentration and positional safety depth.
untested.basis: DeRTa (arXiv:2407.09121) ablates harmful-prefix augmentation, refusal-token optimization (RTO) and their combination (Table 3, Figure 4), but reports no measured gradient-concentration outcome and no demonstrated fixed-data objective-to-gradient-to-depth causal chain; its prose does not give each variant its own refusal-position share (see V6.support[2]). HumorReject (arXiv:2501.13677) holds ORPO fixed and the diffusion Recovery Alignment ablation (V6.support[1]) holds the RL objective fixed, so both vary data or training states rather than the objective. The objective mechanisms in arXiv:2603.04851 and arXiv:2606.04168 are conditional theory. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation records training, measurement and attack coverage, but does not establish this controlled causal chain.

untested.what: Whether additional ordinary training data alone can overcome the proposed objective-induced shallowness.
untested.basis: arXiv:2603.04851 (Section 10.1) argues that, under its formalization, modifying the objective is necessary; it reports no empirical data-scaling experiment. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation has no scaling entry; versions.V6.main_rows_by_operation likewise has no scaling operation.

untested.what: Scale-specific empirical tests below 1B or above 100B, and a controlled model-size sweep of the causal mechanism.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size contains 1-10B, 10-100B and not stated, with no <1B or >100B entry; versions.V6.coverage_by_operation has no scaling entry. The packed size-specific interventions do not establish a scaling law.

wording_issues.issue: The evidence has different causal strength. HumorReject changes response data with ORPO fixed, and the diffusion ablation changes training-state coverage with the RL objective fixed. DeRTa combines data and objective changes. These comparisons do not establish a single universal cause.

The packed outcomes operationalize shallowness differently: vulnerability to Template+Prefill, refusal-token placement, positional KL of further DPO or NPO safety tuning measured against the original instruct model (not a pretrained base model), and vulnerability to contaminated diffusion states. The diffusion result does not test the autoregressive first-response-token mechanism.

The objective explanations require explicit assumptions: prefix-determined harm in the RLHF analysis, or autoregressive consistency and smoothness in the SFT/DPO analysis. The incomplete-learning paper's gradient-concentration account has no measured gradients or comparison of objectives and receives no V6 support verdict.

method_sensitivity.what: With prompts and ORPO fixed, direct refusal versus humorous safe chosen responses changes Llama3-8B-Instruct safety on HEx-PHI Illegal Activity under Template+Prefill from 0.00% to 96.67%. This sensitivity is established for the packed attack and judge setting.

With the RL objective fixed, training only from fully masked starts versus contaminated intermediate states changes LLaDA Instruct ASR from 22.0 ± 1.7% to 1.3 ± 0.6% under Anchoring at tinter=4 on JBB-Behaviors with GPT-4o judging.

method_sensitivity.factor: Joint data augmentation and refusal-token training
method_sensitivity.what: The non-initial refusal-token share in LLaMA3-70B safe responses changes from 20% under vanilla safety training to 50–55% across DeRTa variants. The reported range does not identify the effect of each component separately.

Exact zero late-position harm gradients require prefix-determined harm in the RLHF theorem; shared parameters can still create incidental late-position KL. The SFT/DPO suppression result instead requires autoregressive consistency and smoothness bounds. These are conditional theoretical dependencies, not measured empirical sensitivities.
